Polycab India is India's largest wires and cables manufacturer (~30-31% organised market share) running three compounding engines — W&C core, a fast-growing FMEG segment, and EPC — making it the broadest-spectrum play in India's power-infrastructure capex cycle. Q2FY27 revenue accelerated to +53% YoY (₹9,900cr) with PAT up +43% YoY (₹990cr, 10.0% margin), a marked step-up from +29% growth in FY26; PAT margins have expanded from 9.4% to 10.0% over six quarters, FMEG achieved its first double-digit EBIT margin (10.1%), and working capital is compressed to just 11 days versus management's own 45-50 day target — signalling exceptional execution quality. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary multiple for this capital-intensive name (per Sector Card guidance), Polycab trades at 35× — at the P53 peer percentile among 17 Industrials names — with forward P/E of 38.5× materially below trailing 53.8×, confirming earnings growth is expected and priced in but not at an extreme premium; grading fair, but with the stock at 99.8% of its 52-week range, near-term risk/reward is asymmetric for a new position. The key risk is sustained copper price inflation (+40-45% in H1 FY27) threatening volume demand and margin durability, compounded by UltraTech's entry into the wires market representing the first credible long-term competitive threat to Polycab's market-share dominance.
